ledger.note: 1806: Lübeck becomes a sovereign state. Lübeck 'became a sovereign state at the dissolution of the Holy Roman Empire in 1806' (Lübeck page); it had 'remained a Free Imperial City even after the German Mediatisation in 1803'. The page names no territory; the Bergedorf condominium with Hamburg is the page's own (it sold its share in 1868).

region.text: the city of Lübeck, occupied after the battle of 6 November 1806

ledger.note: 1806: French troops occupy Lübeck. Troops under Bernadotte 'occupied neutral Lübeck after a battle against Blücher on 6 November 1806' (Lübeck page).

1811: the occupation turns into annexation. The Lübeck page says only 'annexed by France from 1811 to 1813'; whether French troops stayed in the city from 1806 to 1811 is on no page opened, so the end is bridged at the annexation.

ledger.note: 1811: France annexes Lübeck. 'Lübeck was annexed by France from 1811 to 1813' as part of the department of Bouches-de-l'Elbe (Lübeck page); the Bouches-de-l'Elbe page: 'It was formed in 1811', capital Hamburg, redivided in 1814 among Hanover, Saxe-Lauenburg, Hamburg and Lübeck. Reviewer eu-20-e (2026-11-01): confidence 2, because the region includes the Bergedorf share, which the Lübeck page does not name for 1811-1813.

ledger.note: 1813: Lübeck is free again. 'Lübeck regained its pre-1811 status in 1813' (Lübeck page); the Congress of Vienna then 'reconfirmed Lübeck's independence' as one of the 39 sovereign states of the German Confederation. Reviewer eu-20-e (2026-11-01): confidence 2, because the region includes the Bergedorf share, which the Lübeck page does not name for 1811-1813.

region.text: Lübeck's share of the Bergedorf condominium

ledger.note: 1868: Lübeck sells its share in Bergedorf to Hamburg. 'Lübeck joined the North German Confederation in 1867. The following year Lübeck sold its share in the bi-urban condominium of Bergedorf to the' Free and Hanseatic City of Hamburg. Cliopatria's Hamburg row already draws Bergedorf, so Hamburg's map does not change.

region.text: the state's outline as it stood in 1870, unchanged to November 1918

ledger.note: November 1918: Lübeck, a free city with no monarch, passes from the Empire's member states to a state of the Weimar Republic. 'After the collapse of the empire following the First World War, Lübeck joined the Weimar Republic as a constituent state' (infobox 'State of the German Empire' and 'State of the Weimar Republic'; 'Abolished by the Greater Hamburg Act: 1 April 1937'). The page gives no month; November 1918 follows the revolution page, which has the revolution in control of 'all large coastal cities' by 7 November. Federal state of the German Empire from 1871 ('The other states retained their own governments but had only limited aspects of sovereignty', German Empire page). Was a dissolve in 1871 into german-empire; moved to November 1918 and the counterpart changed to weimar-republic on the 3 Nov 2026 fix (fx-53 D01, as fx-46 R122 did for Bavaria): the Empire was this state's overlord, not its successor.

certainty.note: No page gives Lübeck's boundary; Bergedorf was a condominium shared with Hamburg, so its frontier is soft throughout.

After the sale of Bergedorf the state is the city with its own land; no page gives the line, but nothing else was shared. 1872-1918 (fx-53): the dossier records no frontier change after 1871; the state keeps its 1870 outline as a federal state of the German Empire.

notes: CLIOPATRIA ROW MISLABELLED: all five shapes (2,551-2,754 km2) are Mecklenburg-Strelitz (Stargard round Neustrelitz and the Ratzeburg land), not Lübeck: the 1806 outline has no cell on Lübeck, and from 1814 it adds the single Lübeck cell to the Strelitz area. The Free City itself is 298 km2 on the German Confederation page. Every verdict is wrong or adjust and the corrections draw Lübeck as a 10 km circle (the city and its land; the page names no villages or Travemünde) plus the Bergedorf condominium (an 8 km circle; Hamburg's Cliopatria row also draws Bergedorf, so the two overlap on purpose until the 1868 sale). Mecklenburg-Strelitz has a dossier of its own, written in this batch (eu-20-e, slug mecklenburg-strelitz, 1806..1871), whose new keyframes take over these Cliopatria shapes minus the Lübeck cell; the orchestrator may prefer to rename the Cliopatria rows. SILENCES: Lübeck's 1815-1866 events, the Landgebiet, Travemünde, Mölln, and whether Bergedorf stayed in the free city's hands under French rule (the annexation event assumes it did, together with Hamburg's). The Bouches-de-l'Elbe page gives no annexation day. Gazetteer: Bergedorf is not a place; Lübeck is. Pages budget: 5 (the fifth unused). REALM OF MEMBER STATES (fx-53 D01, 3 Nov 2026): this state now lives to November 1918 as a federal state of the German Empire, which 'retained their own governments' (German Empire page: 'The other states retained their own governments but had only limited aspects of sovereignty'; 'the Kaiser and all German ruling kings, dukes, and princes abdicated' in November 1918) and the German revolution of 1918-1919 page: 'By the end of the month, the dynastic rulers of all the other German states had abdicated without bloodshed'. Changed: identity.end 1871 -> 1918/11; the 1871 dissolve into german-empire became a 1918/11 dissolve into weimar-republic; successors german-empire -> weimar-republic; last keyframe (free-city-of-lubeck_1870) carried to 1918 ('to'); capital and certainty to 1918. The german-empire dossier no longer gains this land in 1871 nor lists the state as a predecessor, and weimar-republic lists it as a predecessor (fx-53 D02, D04). The hierarchy.csv row free-city-of-lubeck -> german-empire (constituent, 1871-1918) is for the orchestrator. A free city: no abdication and the Lübeck page gives no month for the change; November 1918 follows the revolution page. Statehood ended on 1 April 1937 (Greater Hamburg Act).
